subject: Oceanography
title: Black and White Smokers
description: A 60-second lesson on Black and White Smokers.

hook.text: Towers of mineral-rich water shoot from the seafloor at 400°C—black as chimney smoke.

buildup.text: Seawater seeps into cracks near ridges, heats up, dissolves minerals, and blasts back out as 'smoke.'

discovery.text: Black smokers precipitate sulfide minerals—iron, copper, zinc—building chimneys up to 60 meters tall.

twist.text: White smokers are cooler and deposit lighter minerals—barium and silicon—creating pale chimneys.

climax.text: These vents host unique ecosystems—bacteria, tubeworms, and shrimp found nowhere else on Earth.

punchline.text: Underwater chimneys build oases from boiling mineral soup.

quiz.question: What gives black smokers their dark color?
